subject: arts-music
lesson_title: Concept model A: paint or color media
task_label: Design and communication — First concept model
essential_question: How can understanding materials, techniques, and design help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Build a clear mental model of paint or color media through an explicit worked example, demonstration, text, or phenomenon.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of paint or color media.
Check, revise, or improve work about paint or color media using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about paint or color media.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
task_brief: This is day 2 of "Materials, Techniques, and Design". That is unit 2 in grade 5. Today is a first concept model about paint or color media. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Design a small collection around a shared theme using at least two media. Today helps by working on paint or color media. Your unit also covers drawing tools, paint or color media, collage and printmaking, and three-dimensional construction. Today is for practice. You are scored on finishing and being honest, not on getting it perfect.
primary_task: Look closely at the first artwork about paint or color media before you make anything. Look three times. First, what do you see or hear? Second, how was it put together? Third, how does it make you feel? Name the one choice the artist made to create paint or color media. Now copy just that one part in a small study. Not the whole thing. Write one sentence about what was harder than it looked. Say where the artwork came from. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about paint or color media. It is part of "Materials, Techniques, and Design". Later days in this unit cover other things, like drawing tools. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about paint or color media; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 5, finish on your own. Write a reason for each main choice. If there were two ways to do it, say which one you picked and why.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task uses things you look at (paint or color media). You may use raised or textured materials, very large print, strong colours, or a spoken description instead.
You may use low-smell, low-dust materials, and you can sit or stand to work. Ask for chunkier handles or grips if that helps.
Anything you have to study will also come as plain text, a described version, or a version you can touch.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting paint or color media.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for paint or color media follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for paint or color media, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for paint or color media works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of paint or color media, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking paint or color media mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply paint or color media under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on paint or color media rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
